effect: An AI state now launches sabotage (cutting a power grid, sabotaging a power plant or an oil or gas field) only when its odds of being caught are acceptable, as it already does for covert support to a foreign group. The AI's state-operations rule launched a step whenever the operation was possible, cost at most 10% of its cash and its readiness was 0.25 or more; it never read the operation's own detection chance, though an attributed sabotage costs the sponsor relations and a security grudge that feeds sanctions and crises. The same AI's proxy-support rule refuses when detection exceeds 0.45, plus or minus 0.1 for a hawkish or dovish leader. Now the three sabotage missions use that same test: launched only when the detection chance is at most 0.45 + (hawkish - 0.5) x 0.2. Preparation steps (reconnaissance, access, networks), intelligence theft and counter-intelligence are unchanged. Real-world behaviour: state sabotage is planned for deniability and called off when exposure is likely (Stuxnet; from memory). Day-0 effect: none. No new saved state.
